provenance.claim: mode: numeric-superscript — Cell Press's own announcement: “Cell Press now requires all new and revised submissions [after October 2022] to format citations using the superscript numbered referencing style” (e.g. 'this observation1,2'); Neuron is explicitly named in the list of affected journals.
authorTruncation: “'Et al.' should be used only after 10 author names” — confirmed identically across two independent search retrievals of the same page.

collapseRanges / sortOrder: not independently confirmed with a worked example; inferred from the numbered-superscript system (numbers are necessarily assigned/read in order of appearance, and collation of adjacent numbers is standard practice for such systems) rather than from an explicit statement.

entryTemplates / journalAbbreviation / doiPolicy: left null — cell.com/neuron/information-for-authors and /information-for-authors/figure-guidelines returned HTTP 403 on every direct-fetch attempt in this session; no search excerpt surfaced a verbatim reference-entry pattern for Neuron specifically, and third-party aggregators (manusights.com, Paperpile, EndNote) were excluded as non-primary sources.

formats.minDpi: “For color or grayscale figures, at least 300 dpi is required; for black and white figures, at least 500 dpi; for line-art figures, at least 1,000 dpi at the desired print size.” Encoded minDpi as the 300dpi floor; the 500/1000dpi tiers for B&W/line-art are recorded here rather than modeled (schema has one minDpi field).

maxHeightMm: Neuron's Final File Requirements state “Figures should be a maximum of 6.5 x 8 in (16.5 x 20 cm) to allow for page margins and text” — an overall page-fit maximum, not a single/double-column preset system like Nature/Science use, so only the height (20cm) is encoded in maxHeightMm; the 16.5cm width maximum is recorded here rather than forced into widthPresetsMm.single/double, which would misrepresent it as a column-preset system Neuron does not appear to use.

notes: RETRIEVAL CAVEAT (applies to this entire profile): cell.com returned HTTP 403 to the WebFetch tool on every path attempted in this research session — information-for-authors, article-types, figure-guidelines, star-authors-guide, both PDFs, and the news page. Every 'documented' claim above was corroborated through Google-indexed search-engine excerpts of those official pages rather than a direct primary-source read; entries that only surfaced once, vaguely, or exclusively from a third-party formatting-checker blog were left null instead of guessed.

This is materially lower-confidence sourcing than the Nature and Science entries in this batch (both of which had direct-fetch or browser-session access). The user should independently re-verify against the live cell.com pages before relying on any 'documented' claim here for a hard compliance check.

maxHeightMm (200mm) and the implied max width (165mm) come from Neuron's Final File Requirements PDF and represent an overall page-fit maximum, not a Nature/Science-style single/double-column preset system — Cell Press figures are not laid out on the same fixed-column grid, so widthPresetsMm is left null rather than forcing the 165mm figure into a 'double column' slot it doesn't represent.

The Cell Press numbered-superscript style (October 2022 changeover) explicitly lists Neuron among the affected journals, alongside Cell, Cell Reports, Cell Metabolism, Cell Stem Cell, Molecular Cell, Immunity, iScience, Developmental Cell, and others — all now share the same >10-author et al. rule and superscript in-text format.

Figure resolution is tiered by content type (300dpi color/grayscale, 500dpi black-and-white, 1000dpi line-art) rather than a single floor; minDpi is encoded as the 300dpi floor with the tiers recorded here since the schema has one minDpi field.
